scope: source-bound process ownership inventory, first-process contract and executable characterization; no production process migration

invariants.assessment: No alternate SWAP kernel is introduced. The snow contract is a process seam owned below the single canonical kernel architecture.
Legacy file readers are classified LEGACY_IO and excluded from the target process evaluator. Parameters and forcing are already-parsed inputs.
Parameters, committed state, forcing, results, diagnostics and reconstructible workspace are explicit. snowinco is corrected to DIAGNOSTIC, not physical state.
Snow physical continuation state is only ssnow plus slw. Reporting baseline snowinco is excluded; inactive snow allocates no process state in the target contract.
Process-local reconstructible snow temporaries are separated from persistent state; solver/Newton scratch remains F-SI-owned worker/job state.
Contract uses committed input to candidate output with commit/rollback authority explicitly retained by F-KT. Rollback/replay identity is characterized.
Same committed state plus same forcing reproduces candidate output. No hidden snow solver warm-start state exists in the characterized algebraic process.

The process API carries t0/t1 and does not require midnight. A non-midnight one-day identity is characterized. Generic-duration/subdaily numerical scaling is deliberately not inferred from B1.10 and remains a hold.
Unrounded snow water-storage identity is checked for normal, warm-fresh-snow and deficit-clamp cases with residuals at floating-point roundoff. No mass-tolerance relaxation is introduced.
Inventory explicitly flags module globals, optional state and MultiSWAP-relevant seams. No per-column heavy solver instance or new runtime design is introduced by F-PM01.
Process contracts do not depend on one Richards implementation. Solver-facing processes are held behind abstract hydraulic/solver interfaces owned by F-SI.
The first seam preserves exact B1.10 snow equations and characterizes them source-bound. No physics formula is rewritten in F-PM01.

Direct HeadCalc use was not found in inspected F-PM processes. Legacy h/theta/qrot/gwl and boundary accesses are exposed as solver-internal dependencies requiring a future hydraulic view rather than being copied into new interfaces.
Physical process configuration is classified separately from numerical policy. Snow has no process numerical policy configuration in the first contract.
B1.10 remains the explicit reference oracle. No alternative process behavior is promoted without characterization against it.
The characterization records source identity, compiler/optimization, mass residuals and scope holds. Runtime normal/relaxed/fallback diagnostics remain outside this non-production slice.
Optional macropore, snow, solute and nutrient states are explicitly identified. The target snow contract requires no snow state allocation when snow physics is inactive.
No new .swp, midnight, one-day, MODFLOW or direct-HeadCalc assumption is introduced. Existing B1.10 day-call behavior is recorded as characterization scope, not silently generalized.

holds: Invariant 9 is not a claim of arbitrary-duration snow numerical equivalence; only explicit generic-time interface shape and one-day non-midnight characterization are qualified.
Production process migration remains blocked until an exact shared qualified F-KT05/F-SI05 downstream source basis exists.
